segments.text: The amendment

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: that I offered, Blumenthal 4255, will not be made pending. But I want to emphasize the importance of the amendment and hope that I can work

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: with my colleagues on the substance of it, because it is so profoundly important to fairness
in the

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: workplace and protection of American workers.
My

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: friend and colleague, the senator from Washington, Patty Murray, has spoken on this issue within the last few minutes,
and

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: I joined her in supporting the critical executive order issued by the president called the Fair Pay and Safe Workplaces Executive Order. This effort requires companies doing business by the federal government to disclose

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: whether they violated

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: any of the 14 longstanding labor laws protecting American workers included in this executive

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: order. There's no requirement to disclose a mere allegation or a claim of a violation of one of those laws. Rather, the executive order requires, very simply, disclosure of a determination by a court or administrative body of an actual

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: violation. This executive order, in effect, would be gutted by the National Defense Authorization Act now on

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: the floor of this Congress. And the amendment that I was intending to offer is the very same amendment that was offered in the NDA markup, supported by groups like Easter Seals and Paralyzed Veterans of America
who worry

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: that this language, in this law that we now have before us, will do a damaging injustice to our veterans and constituents with disabilities

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: and thousands of other employees working under federal contracts. And I'm proud to

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: be joined in this effort by not only Senator Murray, but also Senators Franken, Gillibrand, Brown, Sanders,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Lahey, Baldwin, Merkley, Boxer, Casey,
and

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: the ranking member of the committee with jurisdiction over this bill, Senator Jack Reed of the Armed Services Committee, where the presiding officer
and I sit. We

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: really need to

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: ensure that this
executive order,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: the Fair Pay and Safe Workplaces

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: executive order, applies across all federal agencies,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: to all

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: workers, as many as possible at least, strengthening this vital effort to protect them, workers, and taxpayer dollars. It's not only about workers,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: it's also about taxpayer dollars. The laws that are covered here are sort of the bread-and-butter protections
of
all

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: federal workers and all workers generally, like the Americans with

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Disabilities Act, the Family and Medical Leave Act, and the Civil Rights
Act. Other

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: laws may

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: be more obscure, also covered, but they've been around for decades. And this measure and those laws are designed to protect

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: veterans and women from harmful, debilitating discrimination, among other

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: wrongful practices.
Let's be very

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: clear. Most companies
covered by

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: federal contracts, played by the rules, they obey the law.
All they

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: would need to do is literally check a box, confirming that they are in compliance. No big administrative expense, no elaborate bureaucratic hurdles to overcome. Check a box that there has been

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: compliance and the law is

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: fulfilled. For a small subset of companies with compliance
issues, the

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: contracting agency would take information about violations into consideration in the procurement process. Not to bar them--
they can

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: still be considered-- but they would then try to work with the company to make sure it comes into compliance

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: The basic theory of this executive order is a matter of

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: common sense. It's not about blacklisting companies, it's about ensuring that companies that want to do business with the federal government follow the law and provide a safe, equitable, fair workplace. And...

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Companies that violate those laws should not receive taxpayer dollars. Those are the companies we can trust to be partners in carrying out the federal government's work if they obey the law and they are in compliance with it. Companies that violate the law, very bluntly, are creating an unlevel playing field,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: forcing law-abiding companies

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: into an unfair competition for contracts. They can cut corners,
save

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: money by, in effect, skirting
the law,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: and present low-ball offers, and when they
are hired

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: provide

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: poor performance. Again, to the detriment of taxpayers and wasting federal funds.
And,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: of course, it's not just about

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: dollars, the important to taxpayers, but about workers. Every year, tens of thousands of American workers

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: are denied overtime wages, unlawfully discriminated against in hiring and pay. They have their health and safety put at risk by federal contractors who cut those corners on workers' safety or otherwise deny a basic, safe workplace. And...

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: That's another reason that we need full force and effect to this executive order, not the gutting
of it

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: that is contained now in the NDAA before us. Some have called the fair pay executive order one of the most important advances for workers achieved by this administration.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: it is. According to the Department of Labor, one in five Americans are employed by companies that do business with the federal government, an enormous source of leverage requiring compliance with federal protections, not just in letter, but in spirit. We must very simply allow for consistent and appropriate

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: application of this executive order to ensure that

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: workers for contractors under the defense laws have the same protections as other

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: workers. And the NDAA provision that guts this executive order must be removed at some point. It may not happen
in our

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: considering of this measure now.
But

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: my hope is that we can work with colleagues and overcome the potentially harmful effects of this provision. I look forward, in fact, to a collegial effort to make sure that we provide long-term protection to American workers through this executive order.
Thank you,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: Mr. President, and

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: I yield the floor.
